Here’s a calm, simple routine for a healthy adult dog.

Before you leave

Feed a normal meal unless the clinic told you otherwise. Bring water.
Pack leash or harness, poop bags, any records, and a few small treats.
Let your dog potty right before you go.
Keep the morning low-key. A short walk is fine, but skip rough play.
If your dog gets nervous, practice a few quiet sits and treats at the door so the outing starts calmly.

At the clinic

Stay relaxed and use a steady voice.
Keep your dog on leash or in a carrier until staff says otherwise.
Tell the team any recent changes, even small ones, like appetite, energy, stool, or behavior.
Reward calm behavior with treats when it makes sense.
Ask questions before you leave so you understand any next steps.

Afterwards

Give your dog water and a quiet rest period.
Watch the injection site or handling areas for mild soreness, sleepiness, or a little limp if vaccines were given. If the visit was only a checkup, your dog should usually bounce back quickly.
Call the clinic if you see vomiting, trouble breathing, collapse, swelling, or if your dog seems much worse instead of better.

What are the most likely causes for this kind of repeated stiffness?
